# SK1101 — The local is declared on one line and assigned on the next

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A local declared without an initializer is assigned by the very next statement, so two lines carry one declaration.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

`int count; count = Read();` is the C-era habit that a model has read a great deal of, and it costs a reader the one guarantee the joined form gives for free: that the variable is never observable before it holds something. The rewrite is the smallest in this batch — two lines become one, no expression moves and no scope changes. ⚠ **Nothing in the .NET SDK reports it.** Measured on a `net10.0` probe with `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true`, `AnalysisMode=All` and every code-style diagnostic raised to `warning`, `int x; x = 3; return x;` produced `IDE0130` and `CA1822` and nothing about the split. ⚠ **It needs no semantic model, and that is a fact about C# lookup rather than a shortcut**: an identifier written immediately after `T x;` in the same statement list resolves to that local, because a simple name finds the innermost enclosing declaration and nothing can be declared between two adjacent statements. So the rule runs under `--load=loose`, which is the mode an agent's scratch file is analysed in and exactly where this shape arrives.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
int count;
count = Read(source);
```

Write:

```csharp
int count = Read(source);
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **Only the joining half of the issue ships, and cutting the other half was a decision rather than an omission.** The same issue asks for `TooWideLocalVariableScope` — moving a declaration *into* the narrower block that uses it. That rewrite moves a declaration **inwards**, which is the one direction `RewriteGuards` cannot check: both `WouldCollide` and `DeclaredElsewhereInMember` answer the outward question, and a rule shipped in this repository has already emitted a token-equivalent program failing `CS0136` for exactly that blind spot. Half a concept with a guard is worth more than all of it with a fix that breaks builds. The assignment must be the *immediately* following statement in the same statement list, must be a plain `=` — a compound assignment reads the target as well as writing it and cannot be an initializer — and its left side must be the bare identifier, so `this.x = …` and `x.Field = …` are never matched. ⚠ **A mention of the local anywhere inside the assigned value withdraws the finding**, because `int x; x = Parse(s, out x);` is legal and `int x = Parse(s, out x);` is not; `nameof(x)` is caught with it, which costs a finding nobody will miss. A declaration with more than one declarator is excluded — joining one declarator and leaving the other where it was is a different edit — as are `using`, `await using`, `const`, `ref` and any local carrying attributes. A comment between the two lines withdraws the finding rather than being deleted with them. Generated code is excluded.
